title: FULL EVENT: President Trump Delivers Emphatic Remarks at Kalispell, Montana Rally - 10/14/26
summary: Trump rally speech (Oct 2026): inflation is minimal and far below Biden's, tariffs cause wealth not inflation, oil will crash when the Iran war ends, tariff money funds a $5,000 dividend.

assertions.quote: Again, we have very little inflation.

verdicts.note: September 2026 CPI was 3.7 percent and accelerating, above the roughly 2.5 percent average since 1990 and well above the Fed's 2 percent target.

Headline CPI rose 3.7% in the 12 months to September 2026, above every reading in 2024 (max 3.5%) and 2025 (2.3-3.0%) and above the 2019-20 pre-pandemic pace of about 1.5-2.5%; only the 2021-23 spike (peak 9.1% in June 2022) and April-May 2026 (3.8%, 4.2%) were higher in this series.

assertions.quote: we inherited the worst inflation in history. Think of it. And now the last three months we have 1.7.

verdicts.note: CPI inflation peaked at 9.1 percent in June 2022 and was 3.7 percent in September 2026, well below the peak though above target.
The 12-month CPI-U change peaked at 9.1% in June 2022 and was 3.7% in September 2026, less than half the peak.

assertions.quote: they gave us the worst inflation in American history, the highest energy prices in American history

verdicts.note: The 2022 peak of 9.1 percent was the highest since 1981 but below the 14.8 percent of 1980 and the near-20 percent of 1947.

assertions.quote: it's going to end very quickly. And when that happens, your oil is going to come way down.

verdicts.note: A prediction; oil fell quickly after the 1991 Gulf War, but markets may price in a lasting Gulf risk premium and pump prices fall more slowly than they rise.

assertions.quote: But we don't have inflation and tariffs don't cause inflation.

verdicts.note: Studies of the 2018-2019 and 2025 tariffs find near-complete pass-through into import prices and measurable retail price rises on tariffed goods such as appliances, furniture and coffee.

assertions.quote: You know what they cause? Wealth. They cause wealth.

verdicts.note: The 2018-2019 tariffs produced a net welfare loss after counting revenue (Fajgelbaum et al.), and large majorities of surveyed economists say tariffs lower average living standards.

assertions.quote: in order to avoid tariffs, they're all building their plants in here because they don't want to pay tariffs.

verdicts.note: Tariff-jumping investment is a real mechanism (Japanese auto plants in the 1980s), but announced pledges far exceed realized spending and tariffs on inputs deter other investment.

assertions.quote: we're building more factories and plants in the United States right now than at any time in the history of our country.

verdicts.note: Manufacturing construction spending peaked in 2024 on CHIPS and IRA projects and has since declined, and manufacturing employment fell through 2025; pledges are not spending.

assertions.quote: The reason is that we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs and record setting economic success.

verdicts.note: Tariffs bring in roughly 300-400 billion dollars a year while a 5,000 dollar payment to about 260 million adults would cost about 1.3 trillion dollars.

assertions.quote: income for hardworking Americans has soared to the highest level ever recorded.

verdicts.note: Nominal incomes are at record highs, but with CPI at 3.7 percent against wage growth near 3 percent in 2026, real pay for typical workers has been flat to falling this year.

assertions.quote: if I took the tariffs off and let's say we got uh a penny off the cost of your lumber

verdicts.note: Protection does shift some output to domestic mills, but NAHB estimates lumber tariffs add thousands of dollars to a new home and US lumber output has been flat with weak housing starts.
